coordinates.object_orientation: Body length along X, head -X, tail +X, dorsal +Z, paired fins symmetric across Y. Front -Y broadside, side+X toward head, top+Z, perspective(+X,-Y,+Z).

concept.reason: Real complete-ish specimen photograph plus same-species published anatomical restoration provides sufficient wholebody reference.

representation: Conservative complete living fish restoration, not fossil slab or exact individual scan
primary_evidence: NHM species photograph plus Woodward1909 Fig49 restoration and PlateXXXVI Fig1 type NHMUK PV OR4219; identity bridge confirmed Norton et al2026. Photograph caption does not itself give catalogue number: do not assert exact photo/type identity.

context.age: Late Cretaceous, Turonian to possibly Santonian for species
context.locality: Southern England Chalk; type from Lewes, Sussex
context.note: No Lower Cretaceous gombessae morphology or material mixed.

dimensions.basis: Representative species length about600mm reported by NHM and Woodward; NOT measurement of NHM photo. Head+operculum and maximum trunk depth each about1/4 total in Woodward diagnosis. Width and fin envelope inferred.

must_preserve: Short stout head and compact deep trunk with blunt spatulate snout, not Coelacanthus narrow long head.
Head+operculum about25 percent length; maximum trunk depth similar. Large opercular region and modest lateral eyes.
First dorsal ray fin has no fleshy lobe and eight primary rays per Woodward. Second dorsal is lobed and separate.
Paired pectoral and pelvic fins with rounded fleshy bases and fan blades. Anal resembles smaller second dorsal, located slightly farther rearward.
Caudal upper/lower fan lobes roughly balanced, with only subtle short central axial continuation. No elongated Latimeria supplementary tail paddle.
Living skin covers bones and ossified swim bladder; fossil cavities are NOT exterior openings.
Scales/cranial tubercles subtly implied in authored low-poly geometry, not oversized spikes or copied photo texture.
Unknown colors muted and explicitly inferred; not modern coelacanth white spotting.
forbidden: Label historical mantelli as a second distinct species
Mix gombessae, precursor, modernLatimeria or priorCoelacanthus model anatomy
Expose fossil vertebrae, calcified swim bladder or broken body holes on living model
Long central tail whip, generic teleost fork, merged median fins
Photo textures, imported meshes, extra concept images, labels or plinth
